en: Jose Rizal wrote the novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose Spanish colonial abuses in the Philippines.
The Philippine eagle, scientifically named Pithecophaga jefferyi, is the largest eagle in the world and the national bird.
The Supreme Court of the Philippines, led by the Chief Justice, holds the judicial power to interpret the Constitution.
General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, in Kawit, Cavite.
The Ifugao people carved the Banaue Rice Terraces into the mountains of Luzon over two thousand years ago.
Baybayin is an ancient pre-colonial Philippine writing system that uses characters to represent syllables of the Tagalog language.
Dr. Fe del Mundo was the first female student admitted to Harvard Medical School and pioneered pediatric care in the Philippines.
The Ati-Atihan festival in Kalibo, Aklan, honors the Santo Niño with participants painting their faces to mimic the Ati people.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage site protecting diverse marine ecosystems.
Filipino citizens acquire the right and duty to vote in national elections once they reach the age of eighteen.
National Artist Guillermo Tolentino sculpted the Bonifacio Monument in Caloocan and the Obligation statue at the University of the Philippines.
The sampaguita, a fragrant white jasmine flower, was declared the national flower of the Philippines in 1934.
